---
title: "The matrix of pairwise posterior probabilities"
subtitle: "1.13 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Figure 2A and slides 38 and 54"
description: "Pairwise probabilities under alternative orderings of the same units."
---

The cell in row $i$ and column $j$ contains $\pi_{ij} = \Pr(\theta_i > \theta_j \mid Y)$. Since equality has posterior
probability zero in this example, the transposed cell contains $1 - \pi_{ij}$. Under independent normal posteriors,
ordering units by their posterior means places many of the less certain comparisons near the diagonal. The width of
this region also reflects differences in posterior precision. Alternative orderings permute each unit's row and
column together, leaving the underlying probabilities unchanged. The matrix thus distinguishes posterior uncertainty
from the choice of an ordering for presentation.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Six sites, by posterior mean.** C above D, .638, is the least certain direction, and its cell is next to the
  diagonal; A above B (.812) and E above F (.856) follow. Below the diagonal each cell is one minus its mirror: D
  above C is .362.
- **Six sites, by label.** The same matrix, with C above D still at .638: the labels already follow the posterior
  means.
- **League, by label.** Of 435 pairs, the least certain, U19 above U25 at .502, sits 6 cells from the diagonal.
  None of these 10 least certain pairs is next to the diagonal; the farthest is 26 cells away.
- **League, by posterior mean.** The middle-blue cells now form a band: U19 above U25 is next to the diagonal, and
  so are 8 of these 10 least certain pairs; the farthest is 2 cells away.
- **Two imprecise units.** At prior SD .10 the cell in row U22, column U25 is 5 cells from the diagonal, yet its
  probability is only .528: both are small units with posterior SD .089.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The six sites are fictional after-school sites, A to F, from postrank's tutorial data: their normal posteriors for
the reading score are set by hand and taken as given. An evaluation office grades them to set the order of its
visits. The league is that of [Ranking noisy estimates](noisy-league.qmd), with the posterior of
[normal–normal posterior shrinkage](shrinkage.qmd). Two imprecise units can have direction probabilities near one half even when they are far apart in the
ranking. Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Section IV.B, Figure 2A, and slide 38: the heat map of pairwise posterior
probabilities for the first names of KRW's name analysis (KRW call the posteriors beliefs). Slide 54 shows the same
heat map for the firms. KRW put one half on the diagonal by convention; postrank leaves the diagonal empty.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
round(1 - pr_tutorial$one$e[, , "score_A"], 3)   # the six sites' matrix (C, D: 0.638)
1 - pr_tutorial$one$e["C", "D", "score_A"]       # 0.6381632
```
:::
